tail:
### FINDING 1 — def-locally-compact-space — cited results do not establish the sup-metric topology or boundedness used

LOCATION: Definition, lines 81–91

QUOTE: "Give $\mathbb{R}^n$ the product topology, which is the metric topology of $d_\infty$ ([[lem-metrics-on-rn]], [[cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology]]). ... it is bounded ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]), lying inside $B(p, 2)$; so $Q_p$ is compact by [[cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology]]."

DEFECT: Neither cited Statement establishes that the product topology is induced by the sup metric. The first only establishes that the displayed sup formula is a metric; the second identifies the product topology with the Euclidean metric topology and applies Heine–Borel to Euclidean boundedness. The item proves only sup-metric boundedness before invoking that corollary, so both the topology identification and the compactness inference are unlicensed by the cited facts.

EVIDENCE: The Statement of `lem-metrics-on-rn` says, "**Then $d_1$, $d_2$ and $d_\infty$ are metrics on $\mathbb{R}^n$**." The Statement of `cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology` instead introduces "$d_2$ [as] the Euclidean metric" and says, "The product topology on $\mathbb{R}^n$ **is** the metric topology of $d_2$." Its closed-and-bounded characterization is made in that Euclidean-metric context.

SEVERITY: fatal

MINIMAL REPAIR: Replace every occurrence of $d_\infty$ in lines 82–89 by $d_2$. The resulting Euclidean closed ball is closed and bounded in the precise metric used by the cited Heine–Borel corollary.
